{{Short description|Austrian biologist}}
{{Orphan|date=August 2024}}

'''Johannes Fritz''' (born 1967)<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4691-2892 |access-date=2024-02-18 |website=orcid.org}}</ref> is an Austrian [[biologist]] and conservationist. He is known for his work in [[wildlife conservation]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=Johannes Fritz |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Johannes-Fritz |work=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref> especially with [[northern bald ibises]], claiming he has been able to “rewild” 277 ibises in [[Austria]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Cole |first=Margherita |date=2023-08-25 |title=Biologist Teaches Endangered Birds New Migration Path To Save Them From Extinction |url=https://mymodernmet.com/johannes-fritz-teaches-northern-bald-ibis-new-migration-pattern/ |access-date=2024-01-20 |website=My Modern Met |language=en}}</ref> He is the director of the Waldrapp Team<ref>{{Cite news |last=Morelle |first=Rebecca |date=2010-10-27 |title=Follow that microlight: Birds learn to migrate |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-11574073 |access-date=2024-01-20 |work=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> and was involved with the production of [[BBC]]'s ''[[Planet Earth III]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fritz |first=Johannes |title=BBC One - Planet Earth III - Saving the Northern bald Ibis in a changing world |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/articles/2XzhT4BbdxkHXn43Fctc9BB/saving-the-northern-bald-ibis-in-a-changing-world |access-date=2024-01-20 |website=[[BBC]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hruby |first=Denise |date=2018-07-20 |title=Ibis that was extinct in wild taught to migrate by following aircraft |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2018/jul/20/formerly-extinct-ibis-taught-to-migrate-by-following-light-aircraft |access-date=2024-01-20 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Fritz has two sons.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Hruby |first=Denise |title=To Stop an Extinction, He's Flying High, Followed by His Beloved Birds |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/18/world/europe/johannes-fritz-ibises-migration.html |work=[[The New York Times]]|date=18 August 2023 }}</ref>
[[File:Northern bald ibis (Geronticus eremita).jpg|thumb|187x187px|This is a northern bald ibis, also known as a waldrapp.]]

== Education ==
At 20, Fritz enrolled in a biology program at a university. He worked to monitor groups of [[chamois]] and [[deer]].<ref name=":1" /> At 24, studies in various [[Austria]]n universities and worked at the [[Konrad Lorenz Forschungsstelle]] research center.<ref name=":1" />

== Northern bald ibises ==
Since 2004, Fritz's career has centered in the conservation of the northern bald ibis, teaching the birds [[Bird migration|migration paths]] from Austria to [[Italy]].<ref name=":0" />
